attacksRun.attack: Item 4 understates the successor obligation by conditioning it on required-now membership
attacksRun.detail: This was my sharpest line. D-018 item 2 protects D-002's gates, which read alone would make any gate addition a scoped successor. But D-018's own decision-type paragraph names the protected set as the condition-4 required-gate set, and the adopted gate-adding acts D-150 and D-154 both style themselves scoped D-002 condition-4 required-gate-set successor. A row that does not enter required-now does not touch that set, so the draft's conditional matches adopted doctrine.

advisories.title: Item 4 compresses two distinct successor obligations into one slashed phrase where the corpus has an exact adopted formula
advisories.finding: Item 4 says a later act 'is a scoped D-002 / D-086 required-now successor if it adds a row to the required-now set.' The adopted gate-adding acts state these as two obligations discharged together: 'scoped D-002 condition-4 required-gate-set successor, and D-086 successor in the same act' (D-150, D-154). The draft's phrase names both instruments, so nothing false follows, but it blurs which set each one protects — D-002's is specifically the condition-4 required-gate set — in a sentence whose entire function is to tell a later drafter what their act must be.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: The later act is expressly not performed here and gets its own D-000 review, where the precise formula is applied and checked. The conditional itself is doctrinally correct, which is the part that could have been a blocker.
advisories.repair: Adopt the D-150/D-154 wording verbatim: 'is a scoped D-002 condition-4 required-gate-set successor and a D-086 successor in the same act, if it adds a row to the required-now set.'

coordinatorSummary: CONSENT at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with one advisory. Twelve attacks run, one landed and it is advisory-grade. Custody is clean: subject 9c6c75c5 at 0444 unmoved, HEAD never left a7d98c2, governing tree clean, no ## D-156 heading in COORD with D-155 the last adopted entry, and C-D156 unused. All eight cited digests reproduce at both ends. The recording claims hold against live bytes: the ten classes in item 1 set-compare exactly to the candidate's two owns lists and to D-155's adopted leftover list; DR-117's status column still reads OPEN; the gate table is still DR-G01 through DR-G28 with no G29 or above; required-now is 24 in the live condition-4 cell; condition 2 reads 4 of 32 in both places; and D-149 is the correct sibling branch for a leftover grouping. The attack worth reporting is the one that failed. Item 4 conditions the scoped-successor obligation on required-now membership, and D-018 item 2 read alone protects D-002's gates without that qualifier, which would have made the conditional under-inclusive. But D-018's decision-type paragraph names the protected set as the condition-4 required-gate set, and the two adopted gate-adding acts I checked, D-150 and D-154, both style themselves scoped D-002 condition-4 required-gate-set successors. The conditional matches adopted doctrine. The advisory is that item 4 compresses that into 'scoped D-002 / D-086 required-now successor' where the corpus has an exact adopted phrasing naming two obligations and the set each protects; the repair is to copy D-150/D-154 verbatim. One limit on this consent, stated rather than glossed: the draft's input table characterises the Codex leftover verdict as ACCEPT 0/0, and independence bars me from opening it, so I verified its digest and not its content. Three tool-side self-corrections are recorded, including a regex that split EE-7d and would have produced a false MUST-FIX against a clean draft, and a gate-table pattern that matched zero rows and made a prohibition check vacuously pass until I refixed it.
